note: Cross-edition AES-256-GCM payload-codec conformance vectors (#188). A payload sealed by one edition opens in the other under the same key; the byte layout (nonce||ciphertext||tag) and metadata tags are identical. Generated from the Python edition; the TS edition MUST reproduce data_hex from key+nonce+plaintext and MUST open data_hex back to plaintext_hex.

subject_scoped.note: Subject-scoped crypto-shred vectors (#715 slice 4). A subject-scoped payload's key id is 'tfsubj1:<b64url(s1)>,<b64url(s2)>,...' and its AES key is SHA-256(record_key(s1)||record_key(s2)||...). Both editions MUST reproduce data_hex from the record keys+nonce+plaintext, MUST open data_hex back to plaintext_hex under the same combined key, and MUST route a destroyed subject to the DISTINCT shred error (never plaintext). A no-subject execution keeps the shared-key vectors above byte-for-byte, so 'no subject unchanged' is proved by the shared vectors reproducing identically under the subject-scoped codec's fallback path.
subject_scoped.kid_format: tfsubj1:<b64url(subject_id) no-padding, comma-joined in resolved order>
subject_scoped.combine: SHA-256 of the concatenated 32-byte per-subject record keys, in kid order

decode_after_shred.note: Using the single-subject-seal-unseal vector: destroy the record for 'subject-0001', then decode of its data_hex MUST raise the distinct subject-key-shredded error, never plaintext, never an empty result.
